summary: One machine, one Run occupying it for forty minutes, and one Run queued behind it that needs two things the machine cannot simply take: an image at a registry that serves nothing to an anonymous reader when it is asked to prepare one, and a corpus in an object store that answers only a signed read. Mercator holds the registry account and the object-store key and hands the machine neither. What it hands over is one pull of that one digest and one read of that one version, each naming the operation it was minted for, the workspace whose content it reaches, and the moment it stops being accepted, and both windows close long before the queued Run finishes. The occupant's own image is public, and it is fetched with nothing at all, because minting material for content any anonymous reader can have would put an account on a machine that never needed one. What this world does not state is the launch. Only the preparation seam consults the registry here, so an image already on the machine is run without presenting anything, which is right, and an image the sweep never reached would be pulled anonymously at launch, which is mercator#221 and is licensed rather than caught. The failure this states is the Mercator every version before it was: PrepareImageCommand.RegistryCredential and PrepareArtifactCommand.SourceCredential declared and populated by nobody, so the node runs a bare pull and an unauthenticated GET, and the only way a private image ever reaches a rented host is a registry password written onto it that outlives every fetch it was ever needed for.
